region: the heartland, the empire's green river country: Tolling is its start, where every heartland skill is met once at tiers 1 to 2, close to a bank, and nothing is best past level 15

places.name: Tolling
places.why: the crossroads of four roads on dry ground above the river and its bridge; one of everything a new player needs
places.foundBy: every character wakes here, in the dead-house under the bell tower
places.hook: the bell tower over the graves as you come up out of the dead-house; then the square's stalls

places.name: The church close
places.why: the chapel, the bell tower and the graves together on the terrace's highest corner

places.name: Widdermill
places.why: the river runs fastest past the terrace's north end; the town's grain is ground here
places.foundBy: Hollow lane runs to it; the wheel is seen from the town's north edge; the miller's errand
places.hook: the wheel turning against the river

places.name: The quarry
places.why: the chapel's and church house's stone came from here; copper and ironstone show in its faces
places.foundBy: the quarry track off the west road past Edda's house; the carter sends you
places.hook: a raw grey cut in the heath, a cart and a crane at its lip

places.name: Sour Hollow
places.why: a damp hollow where someone dumped a leaking cask of vitriol; the mites breed in it
places.foundBy: seen from Palmerway as a yellow-stained dip 15 tiles north of the road; Corvin's and Wenna's mite tasks
places.hook: sickly yellow ground and a split cask in green heath

places.name: The toll-house
places.why: Palmerway was a toll road; kept for Tolling's inn
places.hook: the toll bar lying broken in the verge, and the board of old tolls

places.name: The monument's plot
places.why: the church raises monuments along the empire's roads; the first on Palmerway
places.foundBy: on Palmerway, seen from the toll-house; Brother Hollis
places.hook: four founts round a tall stone

places.name: The waygate
places.why: where Palmerway crests the heath ridge and leaves the start area; the wardens watch the road
places.foundBy: the end of Palmerway, on the skyline from about 60 tiles back
places.hook: a gatehouse on the crest with flags, and the land dropping away to the lake beyond

places.name: The fishers' landing
places.why: the one place on Wennow where boats are kept; the fishers who pulled the player out
places.foundBy: The Bell, step 4; the south-shore path from the Sere road
places.hook: boats and a jetty, and the town's roofs and tower across the water

places.name: The dry rise
places.why: the first dry ground south of the mere, where the green ends; the first climb
places.foundBy: the path up from the landing; seen from the south shore
places.hook: a rock tor with a cairn, and gravel instead of grass

places.name: The edge farm
places.why: the last green farm on the Sere road, where the meadow meets the gravel
places.foundBy: on the Sere road, 50 tiles past the town
places.hook: a longhouse in a walled yard; field walls broken where the gravel took the fields

heights.name: The town's terrace
heights.profile: level ground 1.5 to 2.5 over the river (0.1), varying by about a tile across the town; a grassy bank of about 1.5 down to the river on the east over 4 to 6 tiles; long gentle slopes elsewhere; no cliff, no knoll
heights.why: the town sits dry above the river

heights.name: The quarry
heights.profile: a pit about 12 by 10 cut into the heath; bare rock faces about 2.5 high on the north and west holding the rocks; a cart ramp in on the south
heights.why: Mining's rocks need a face to stand in

heights.name: Sour Hollow
heights.profile: a bowl about 12 across with gentle sides; stained ground at the bottom round the cask
heights.why: the mites' place reads as a place: a dip you look down into

heights.name: The dry rise
heights.profile: gravel slopes of about 1 in 8 from Wennow's south shore; a tor of rock about 2 high on top with the cairn; the far side falls slowly south into the dry
heights.why: the first climb, and the view of the mere from its far side

heights.name: The heath ridge
heights.profile: a broad swell between Wennow's east shore and Knellmere's fens, its crest along this line; slopes of about 1 in 10, 40 to 50 tiles each side; heath, no rock face
sees: the lake opening ahead (the lake road's area)
heights.why: leaving the start area is a crest seen from far off, with the waygate on it

heights.name: The Wenn's glen
heights.profile: the Wenn cutting through the ridge's south end; steep banks about 3 high for about 20 tiles
heights.why: the river needs a way through the ridge

Palmerway over the waygate's crest; Wenna's fen rat errand to the reed fens; The Bell's ending points at the drowned belfry; fishing moves there from tier 2
